newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt to call confidence vote over decree.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt to call confidence vote over decree.

text.p: The Italian government plans to call a vote of confidence in the lower house of parliament to ensure passage into law of a cabinet decree covering development projects, Transport Minister Claudio Burlando said on Tuesday.

Burlando told reporters the government had decided at a cabinet meeting to introduce the confidence vote to help speed into law a decree which will release funds for the development of rundown industrial areas in Milan and Naples.

Ratification of the decree has been threatened by filibustering tactics from opposition parties. Victory in the vote would ensure the legislation passes while defeat would bring down Italy's centre-left government.

The decree is due to expire on November 20 unless it has been passed into law by then. It cannot be resubmitted as a result of a recent Constitutional Court ruling banning the practice of successive cabinets of re-issuing expiring decrees.

Under parliamentary rules, at least 24 hours must elapse between the announcement of the confidence motion and the actual vote. It will be the third confidence vote the government has faced since taking office in May.

Last week Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition won a confidence vote over a decree covering troubled Banco di Napoli. Prodi does not enjoy a majority in the lower house of parliament but is supported there by the hardleft Communist Refoundation.
